RESEARCH RAN TO COMPLETION. notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block at 06:37 ET superseding one at 06:27, so `truncated` is false and nothing here is reconstructed from fragments. candidates.jsonl held 11 lines for 7 distinct symbols; the last line per symbol was taken, which for DG, BCC, GLD and MDT is the version corrected by the research phase's own 06:31 self-audit.

WEIGHTING — four of seven ideas are position management, and that is deliberate rather than thin research. Five open longs carried NO STOP AT ALL, and fixing that was the highest-value work available: CCJ and LCII are closed, GLD and BCC are amended with a stop and a cut target. Only three (PFE, DG, MDT) are new risk, which is what the correlation cap should be read against.

TARGETS WERE CORRECTED DOWNWARD, NOT NUDGED UP. The research phase's self-audit mapped trailing highs by window and found four of its own targets anchored to highs six to nine months old: BCC 90.00 -> 88.00 and GLD 440.00 -> 437.00 were cut, and DG and MDT kept their targets only with the intervening hurdle (134.13 / 95.41) named in key_risk and trimmed at. Every ratio below was recomputed here from the final entry, target and downside.

RATIOS CLUSTER JUST ABOVE THE FLOOR AND THAT DESERVES SUSPICION: BCC 2.02, DG 2.05, MDT 2.18, GLD 2.29 against a 2.0 swing floor, and PFE 2.54 against a 2.5 long-term floor. The mitigating fact is that every stop clears its ATR floor with room (BCC 2.59, DG 2.36, MDT 2.28, GLD 2.12 ETF-adjusted against floors of 2.0/2.0/2.0/1.8), so the ratios were not manufactured from the stop side. BCC's claimed edge over its random-walk baseline is +0.8 points (0.34 vs 0.332) — the thinnest on the page, and its key_risk says it is a hold rather than an add.

SKEW — nothing intraday, one long_term, no small cap, no crypto, no futures, no event contract. Each has a logged reason and none of them is 'ran out of time': with the FOMC on Wednesday and the freshest honest prices being Monday's close, no same-session setup cleared the bar; Kalshi returned zero Fed/CPI markets so no event contract could be priced; and `history BTC-USD` fails while `history BTC` silently returns an equity, so there was no ATR for a crypto or crypto-futures idea.

CORRELATION — four of seven ideas name the 2026-09-16 FOMC as the catalyst, which looks like a concentration and partly is not: DG and MDT want a hawkish statement (defensive rotation), while GLD and BCC want a dovish one (real yields, mortgage rates). Read as one rate-path bet the book is close to flat on the decision itself; read as sector exposure the defensive-rotation leg is DG plus MDT, which is inside the cap of 3.

PRICES — every `last_price` is the 2026-09-14 close, re-quoted at synthesis and unchanged from research. The session was pre-market with an age of 874 minutes: that is a closed market, not stale data. No live or intraday price was available to any idea here.

SOURCES THAT FAILED: (1) `macro` markets block — SPX, NDX, DJI, RUT, VIX, /ES, /NQ, DXY, gold and WTI all ok:false on Yahoo HTTP 429 and Finnhub refusing index CFDs, so there is NO index level and NO VIX read in market_context; FRED rates and coingecko crypto were fine. (2) Kalshi `events` returned count:0 for Fed, Fed decision, interest rate, CPI and recession, and unrelated tennis markets for FEDDECISION — no event contract was captured, and the three FOMC contracts open from prior runs were deliberately not amended blind. (3) `short` (api.nasdaq.com) ReadTimeout on every symbol and every attempt — NO short-interest or days-to-cover crowding check on any idea. (4) `implied` (Yahoo options) HTTP 401 — NO target was tested against the options-implied move; targets rest on window-mapped price structure and, for PFE, on filed guidance.

NOT CHECKED: Robinhood availability was not verified at runtime for any instrument, as config/universe.md asks. All seven are large-cap US-listed equities or a major ETF so the risk is low, but it was not checked.

OPEN POSITIONS NOT ADDRESSED — of the 12 open rows in prior context, four were acted on (CCJ, LCII, GLD, BCC) and two were reviewed and deliberately left alone (DVN and SVRA, both already correctly stopped and neither confirmed nor broken). The remaining rows — NKE, LULU, the SPY short and the TLT sell — were not reached this run and carry no new instruction here.

SIX IDEAS WERE RESEARCHED TO COMPLETION AND REFUSED rather than published: FDX and XLV (2:1 unreachable from any honest level), GIS (cleared only at exactly 2.00 on a stop that was not a level, and prints before a reader could act), the SMH short (target sat below a four-month base at 503.63), ISRG (both roads to 2:1 required either a May high or a stop inside the September low cluster), and CEG/VST (no valuation anchor defensible from a filing). ISRG is on the watchlist and is the first thing to re-check tomorrow.

TRACK RECORD CONTEXT: 0 of 6 closed trades have hit target, average -3.9%. Six is noise, not a verdict, and it is not being over-fitted — but it is the reason today's highest-value work was putting stops under stopless positions rather than adding new ones.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Seven ideas in, six out. **Cut MDT** (was rank 4): its 105.50 target is not set under the relevant high the way every other target on this page is — it IS the 180-day high, confirmed against 180 freshly fetched daily bars, and trimming it to match the page's own rule puts the ratio at exactly 2.00, the construction this same run refused GIS for. MDT also had to clear 95.41 first, a level it has not traded above since 2026-03-24, so the trade carried two ceilings with the exit as the second; and it was the weaker half of the DG/MDT hawkish-rotation pair, since DG makes its six-month high the entry trigger where MDT bought 2% beneath it. It is on the watchlist with a trigger, not deleted. **Downgraded PFE 4 to 3**: two of its three evidence items cite the identical 8-K URL — the valuation_anchor is arithmetic performed on the primary_document, not a second confirmation — and the 12x exit multiple behind the 34.50 target is asserted with no peer or historical anchor shown; at 11x the ratio falls to 2.16 and misses the long-term floor. **Downgraded DG 4 to 3**: its dated_catalyst is the FOMC, shared with the rest of the page and not a confirmation of a dollar store, and its own key_risk concedes revisions and insider activity both point the other way. **Downgraded BCC 3 to 2**: its dated_catalyst is a peer's print that the same idea's key_risk names as the principal downside, and a risk cannot also be counted as evidence for the direction. **CCJ and LCII kept unchanged as exits**, with one real defect fixed — LCII's THO source URL did not resolve and was replaced with a reachable record of the same date, which the red team re-fetched and confirmed (THO 2026-09-22 bmo, consensus EPS 0.9159).

TWO CLASSES OF MECHANICAL FAILURE HERE ARE ARTIFACTS, AND SAYING SO IS NOT SOFTENING THEM. (1) The `fail` verdicts on CCJ and LCII are structural: an exit has no target and no stop, so direction_consistency, risk_reward and stop_distance cannot pass, and the enforce step will demote both to the watchlist even though 'close this position' is the instruction. If they land on the watchlist, read them as closes, not as things to watch. LCII's `earnings_date` failure likewise compares its 2026-09-22 catalyst against LCII's own next print on 2026-10-28; the catalyst is a THO read-across and the report's date is the correct one. (2) The spread failures (DG 8.88%, BCC 24.50%, MDT 5.14%, LCII 15.72%) were pre-market indications captured at 06:39-06:40 ET with no depth behind them — BCC's 'bid 72.50 / ask 92.74' is not a tradeable market in any sense. Re-quoting the same source during the red team returns no bid/ask at all for all seven symbols, so those figures are what was true at 06:40 and nothing more. No level was altered to make a spread check pass, and nothing here is a reason to trade at market: every entry on this page is a limit or a stop-limit and should stay one.

WHAT THE RED TEAM DID NOT CUT, AND WHY NOT. GLD was left alone: its +0.12R expectancy and 3.6-point claimed edge are thin, but it is an amendment putting a stop under an already-filled position rather than new risk, and killing it would leave the position stopless, which is worse than holding it on a thin edge. The four surviving swing ideas still cluster just above their floors and the book's expectancies are small (DG +0.22R, GLD +0.12R, BCC +0.03R); with MDT gone the FOMC exposure is one hawkish expression (DG) against two that want the other outcome (GLD, BCC), which is closer to flat on Wednesday than to a directional bet. Read the residual as three thin idiosyncratic positions, not as a rate view. Validation demoted 4 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 2 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

market_context.summary: A rotation, not a liquidation. August CPI came in at +0.40% MoM (index 334.131 vs 332.813, ~4.9% annualised) and the 2-year at 4.63% sits 100bp above effective fed funds at 3.63% — the front end is pricing tightening, not easing, with unemployment unchanged at 4.1% and no labour-market offset to force cuts. The 2026-09-14 tape was consistent with that: long-duration growth sold (CEG -7.09%, VST -5.16%, CCJ -3.54%, SMH -4.75%), EM sold (EEM -2.73%), gold sold (GLD -1.49%), defensives bid (DG +3.68%, MDT +3.12%, XLV +1.45%) — while SPY fell only 0.45%. The dominant dated event is the FOMC decision on Wednesday 2026-09-16 at 14:00 ET, verified against the Fed's own calendar (the Sep 15-16 meeting), with Lennar's Q3 print landing the same afternoon. Caveat on this summary: no index level and no VIX print could be fetched this run, so the regime read rests on single-name closes, FRED rates and sector ETFs rather than on breadth or volatility.

recommendations.thesis: Read from the primary document rather than a summary of it: the EX-99 to Pfizer's 2026-08-04 8-K guides full-year 2026 revenue of $60.5-62.5B and adjusted diluted EPS of $2.80-3.00, with Q2 revenue of $15.0B, Q2 adjusted diluted EPS of $0.77, and $0.86 per share of dividends paid in the first half. At the 2026-09-14 close of 27.72 that is 9.56x the $2.90 guidance midpoint and a 6.21% yield on $1.72 annualised — a $158.0B company priced as though the earnings base is temporary. Twelve times that midpoint is $34.80; the target is 34.50.
recommendations.key_risk: The patent cliff is the reason the multiple is 9.6x and it is a real reason, not a mispricing — the loss-of-exclusivity wave through 2027-2030 is what the market is discounting, and pipeline replacement is the whole question. The 6.21% yield is a warning as much as a payment: it is the level at which the market starts pricing some probability of a cut, and a cut would break both legs of this thesis at once. **Explicit invalidation** (required for long_term, and it is not 'the price fell'): full-year adjusted diluted EPS guidance cut below roughly $2.40, or any reduction in the quarterly dividend. Either one means the earnings base is not durable and the position closes regardless of price.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that 9.6x is not cheap for an asset whose earnings are contractually scheduled to fall, so the multiple is correct and the yield is a trap. What answers it is the arithmetic of the entry rather than a rebuttal: the thesis does not need the multiple to be wrong, only for $2.90 of EPS not to become less than about $2.30. The bear case of 23.00 prices roughly that — an eroded earnings base at a still-depressed multiple, below the 180-day low of 23.62, on a 7.5% yield. Against a 34.50 target that is 2.54 to 1, and only from 26.29 or lower, which is precisely why the accumulation zone sits under the 50-day rather than at the 27.72 market. The idea has to be bought right or not at all. **Red team adds the weakness the author did not name**: the 12x exit multiple is asserted, not anchored. No peer multiple, no historical range for PFE's own multiple, and no re-rating precedent was shown for it — so while the bear case of 23.00 is defended (an eroded base at a multiple the market is already paying), the 34.50 target rests on a round number with 'conservatively' in front of it. At 11x the target is 31.90 and the ratio from a 26.29 entry falls to 2.16, below the 2.5 long-term floor. The ratio is therefore load-bearing on an assumption rather than on the arithmetic the rest of the thesis is built from.

evidence.detail: Read the EX-99 press release attached to Pfizer's 8-K filed 2026-08-04 (pfe-6282026xex99.htm). Verbatim FY2026 guidance: revenue $60.5 to $62.5 billion, adjusted diluted EPS $2.80 to $3.00. Q2 2026 revenue $15.0B, adjusted diluted EPS $0.77, $4.9B returned as dividends or $0.86 per share in H1 2026.

Method shown: 27.72 close / $2.90 guidance midpoint = 9.56x. $0.86 H1 dividends annualised to $1.72 / 27.72 = 6.21% yield. Market cap $157.99B on 5,699.44M shares. Target = 12x the $2.90 midpoint = $34.80, taken conservatively at 34.50. Bear case = an eroded base near $2.40 at ~9.5x, which is 23.00, below the 180-day low of 23.62 and a 7.5% yield.

First accumulation tranche is the 50-day SMA at 26.34, not a round number; 180-day range 23.62-29.21 with price 5.1% off the high, and ATR14 0.555 (2.0%). The lower tranches at 25.00 and 24.00 sit toward the bottom of that observed range.

Every other idea deliberately sets its objective *under* the relevant high — DG 156.00 under a 158.23 high, BCC 88.00 under 88.43, GLD 437.00 under 437.42 — and MDT's 105.50 is not under its 180-day high, it IS its 180-day high (verified against 180 fetched daily bars: range_high 105.50). So the ratio clears only because the target sits at resistance rather than in front of it. That compounds with the structure the key_risk already admits: 95.41 is the 30/60/90/120-day high and MDT has not traded above it since 2026-03-24, so the trade has to clear two ceilings and the second one is the exit. DG is the same hawkish-FOMC defensive-rotation bet and is the better-built half of the pair — it makes the six-month high its entry trigger where MDT buys 2% beneath it — so the weaker of the correlated two goes. Nothing here says the rotation is wrong; it says this expression of it is not a 2.18 trade.
